original_question: Can the finite-interval analytical characterization problems for fractional integrals and derivatives be extended from bounded intervals to functions defined on the positive real semi-axis and on the whole real line, while preserving the same notions of admissible fractional integrals, associated fractional derivatives, and desiderata-based operator structure?
target_in_paper: Section 2.4, Open Problem 4, read together with Open Problems 1-3 and the setup in Sections 2.1-2.2. Open Problem 4 states: consider the previously formulated finite-interval problems in the case of functions defined on the positive real semi-axis and on ℝ. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main thrust of the target problem: the paper asks to extend the finite-interval characterization program for one-parameter fractional integrals and derivatives from the finite-interval setting to the positive real semi-axis and to ℝ, while keeping the desiderata-based viewpoint. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s target is not a generic extension from bounded intervals to unbounded domains; it is specifically Open Problem 4, which imports the three immediately preceding finite-interval problems from Section 2.4. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

Those imported problems should be spelled out: (1) characterize the fractional integrals satisfying the desiderata of Section 2.1; (2) characterize all families of fractional derivatives associated with the finite-interval Riemann-Liouville fractional integrals through the 1st Fundamental Theorem of fractional calculus; and (3) deduce a general form of the fractional integrals and derivatives in the sense of those desiderata. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

The operator families are one-parameter linear families {I^α}_{α≥0} and {D^α}_{α≥0}; the draft does not explicitly state the one-parameter nature, linearity, or the order range α≥0 used in Section 2.1. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

The desiderata should be named explicitly as HL1-HL6: linearity; semigroup law for I^α; left-inverse relation D^α∘I^α=Id; existence of the limits as α→0 and α→1; D^0=Id; and D^1 equal to the first-order derivative. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

The finite-interval reference model in Section 2.2 is the interval [0,1] without loss of generality, and Theorem 1 singles out the Riemann-Liouville integrals under stronger assumptions CM1-CM4; the refined question should stay tied to that exact finite-interval program rather than a looser bounded-interval generalization. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

For the derivative side, the paper’s concrete finite-interval examples are the Riemann-Liouville, Caputo, Hilfer, and more general n-th level derivatives, with n-th level derivatives shown to be left inverses on X_FT; that associated-derivative mechanism is part of the intended scope behind Open Problem 2. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

The draft risks sounding as if it also targets the separate general fractional integrals/derivatives (GFI/GFD) program, but in the paper those are distinct later open problems, namely Open Problems 6-10 and especially 8-9; Open Problem 4 is about the one-parameter FC operators discussed in Sections 2.1-2.2. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))
refined_question: Can one extend to functions defined on the positive real semi-axis (0,+∞) and on ℝ the finite-interval program of Section 2.4(1)-(3), by characterizing the one-parameter linear families {I^α}_{α≥0} of fractional integrals that satisfy the desiderata HL1-HL6 of Section 2.1, characterizing all one-parameter linear families {D^α}_{α≥0} of fractional derivatives linked to the corresponding integral family through the 1st Fundamental Theorem of fractional calculus D^α∘I^α=Id, and determining the general form of such fractional integrals and derivatives on these two domains? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))
justification: Open Problem 4 in Section 2.4 is the nearest official formulation: it literally asks to consider, on the positive real semi-axis and on ℝ, the problems formulated immediately above. Those preceding problems are Open Problems 1-3 on the same page, concerning characterization of fractional integrals satisfying the Section 2.1 desiderata, characterization of all derivative families associated with the finite-interval Riemann-Liouville integrals via the 1st Fundamental Theorem of FC, and deduction of a general form of the corresponding integrals and derivatives. The nearby context that fixes the intended meaning is Section 2.1, where the desiderata HL1-HL6 are stated for one-parameter families of real order α≥0, and Section 2.2, where the finite-interval model is developed: Theorem 1 gives the uniqueness of the Riemann-Liouville integral family under stronger assumptions, and Theorem 4 shows that n-th level derivatives are examples of associated derivative families. Because the paper treats GFIs/GFDs as a separate later topic with their own open problems, the refined question should not broaden Open Problem 4 to include them. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))
